learningGoals: Understand that 10 ones make one group of ten. 🌟
Identify tens and ones in teen numbers, like seeing 14 as 1 ten and 4 ones. 🧩
Count larger groups of everyday objects accurately without losing track. 🍎
teachingTips: Encourage counting everyday items like grapes, spoons, or toys up to 20. 🍇
Make a bundle of 10 pencils or sticks to physically show what 'one ten' looks like. 🖍️
Keep practice positive! If they skip a number, gently count together from the beginning. 🥰
Ask 'How many?' frequently during daily routines to make math a natural and fun habit. ⏰

funActivities.title: Bundle the Sticks 🪵
funActivities.description: Collect 20 small twigs or matchsticks. Help your child count out 10 and tie them with a rubber band to make '1 ten'. Then, use the extra sticks as 'ones' to build numbers like 11, 12, and 13!

funActivities.title: Snack Time Counting 🍿
funActivities.description: Give your child a small bowl of snacks like raisins, peanuts, or cereal. Ask them to make one group of 10, and then count how many are left over to find the total.

funActivities.title: Toy Parking Lot 🚗
funActivities.description: Line up 11 to 20 toy cars, dolls, or building blocks. Point to them one by one and count aloud together. This helps build focus and accurate one-to-one counting skills!
